# BERT vs GPT: Key Differences

## Architecture

| Feature | BERT | GPT |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Architecture** | Encoder only (Transformer) | Decoder only (Transformer) |
| **Directionality** | **Bidirectional** (reads left & right) | **Unidirectional** (reads left to right) |
| **Attention** | Masked self-attention (sees full context) | Causal self-attention (sees only previous tokens) |

---

## Pre-training Objectives

- **BERT**: 
  - **Masked Language Modeling (MLM)** — predicts randomly masked words in a sentence
  - **Next Sentence Prediction (NSP)** — predicts if two sentences follow each other

- **GPT**: 
  - **Autoregressive Language Modeling** — predicts the *next* word given all previous words

---

## Primary Use Cases

- **BERT**: Best for **understanding** tasks
  - Text classification, sentiment analysis
  - Named Entity Recognition (NER)
  - Question answering (extractive)
  
- **GPT**: Best for **generation** tasks
  - Text generation, chatbots
  - Summarization, translation
  - Code generation

---

## Key Conceptual Difference

- **BERT** = "Fill in the blank" → *understands* context from both directions
- **GPT** = "What comes next?" → *generates* text sequentially

---

## Other Differences

| | BERT | GPT |
|---|------|-----|
| **Developer** | Google | OpenAI |
| **Fine-tuning** | Typically fine-tuned for specific tasks | Can be used via prompting (few-shot/zero-shot) |
| **Model scaling** | BERT-base (110M), BERT-large (340M) | GPT-3 (175B), GPT-4 (rumored ~1T+) |
| **Input/Output** | Input → Label/Span | Input → Generated text |

---

## Simple Analogy

> **BERT** is like a *reading comprehension* student — it reads the whole passage and answers questions about it.
> 
> **GPT** is like a *storyteller* — it writes the next sentence based on everything it has written so far.

Both are foundational models in NLP, and many modern models combine ideas from both approaches.
